title_as_printed: Learning potential and visuospatial memory could predict amyloid-beta positron emission tomography positivity in amnestic mild cognitive impairment

registry_codes.Sample_N_Approx: 64 - 31 Abeta-PET negative/33 Abeta-PET positive, all patients with amnestic MCI and all analysed. The total of 64 is printed in the abstract ("64 patients with aMCI (31 Abeta-PET (-) and 33 ())", plus sign lost in extraction), again at the head of the results

Task_Type.reason: The discrimination task is amyloid-PET status within aMCI only; there is no healthy-control group, so this is a biomarker-subtype task, not MCI vs HC.

Category.reason: The analysed predictors are neuropsychological tests (C5), which the registry codes. Amyloid PET (C1) is the reference label being predicted. Whether a label-only modality counts as a data domain is a judgement, so omitting C1 is at most the omission of a secondary domain.
Category.quote: Patients underwent Aβ-PET scans using 18F-florbetaben and the Seoul Neuropsychological Screening Battery.

Validation_Type.reason: Logistic regression and ROC were fitted and evaluated in the full sample of 64, with no CV, test set or external data (absence of reporting = V2).

Sample_N_Approx.quote: This cross-sectional study included 64 patients with aMCI (31 Aβ-PET (-) and 33 (+))

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Single memory clinic (Pusan National University Hospital), no ADNI data.
